teams.heading: Fiji fall to three straight defeats following 17-33 Scotland loss
teams.body: Fiji are enduring a challenging period, currently on a run of three straight defeats. In their last five games, the Flying Fijians have secured only one victory. Across those same five matches, the team suffered four defeats. Their most recent performance was a 17-33 home loss to Scotland during the Nations Championship group stage in July 2026. This run leaves them sitting 12th of 12 teams on the log.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick recalls Maro Itoje to England squad for autumn preparations
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has recalled lock Maro Itoje to a 36-man England training squad at Pennyhill Park after the second-rower was rested during the summer series. Itoje, who is expected to reclaim the captaincy from the injured Jamie George, missed the July fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina to take his first proper break in a decade. Prop Fin Baxter also returns following 10 months out with a foot injury, but Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant must prove their form in the Premiership before earning selection.

teams.heading: High Court allows landmark concussion lawsuits as France face global scrutiny
teams.body: The UK High Court has allowed landmark lawsuits over neurological injuries to proceed, a decision with major ramifications across the global game. While the legal action primarily targets governing bodies in the UK, the ruling ensures that concussion protocols and long-term player welfare remain under intense scrutiny across all major rugby nations. As France prepare for the upcoming autumn internationals, the ongoing legal battle ensures the sport's safety standards will be a dominant talking point.

teams.heading: Former Ireland lock Ryan Caldwell publishes memoir detailing harrowing post-rugby spiral
teams.body: Former Ireland second-row Ryan Caldwell has opened up about his harrowing descent into addiction, depression, and imprisonment following his retirement from professional rugby. In his upcoming autobiography, White Lines: a Rugby Life Broken and Rebuilt, the former Ulster, Bath, and Exeter enforcer details the physical toll of chronic hip injuries and a final concussion that precipitated his mental health spiral. Now teaching meditation and breathwork, Caldwell reflected on his recovery journey, noting: "I had no love for myself … now I have peace."

lead.why: The raw and poignant interview detailing former Ireland lock Ryan Caldwell's post-retirement struggles and upcoming book is the day's most prominent story.

teams.heading: WRU officials propose radical restructure that could replace Ospreys and Scarlets
teams.body: Wales face a pivotal six months as the WRU prepares a radical overhaul of the professional game. Workshops beginning in December will determine licensing for just three or four clubs, leaving the Ospreys and Scarlets at risk of extinction or a forced merger. Internal discussions include replacing both historic teams with an entirely new West Wales outfit. Although a final decision is expected by March, the governing body insists it is entering the process in good faith despite mounting pressure from fans.

lead.why: The potential collapse or merger of the Ospreys and Scarlets represents an existential shift for the professional game in Wales.

teams.heading: Pablo Matera scores twice as Argentina draw 28-28 against Australia in Mendoza
teams.body: Los Pumas recovered from a 14-point deficit to secure a 28-28 draw against Australia in Saturday's second test in Mendoza. Pablo Matera crossed for two tries, while Ignacio Mendy and Ignacio Ruiz also scored to help the home side take a late lead. Argentina played the final 10 minutes with 13 men after Lucio Cinti and a teammate received yellow cards, but they held on to avoid a defeat following the loss in Jujuy.

teams.heading: Les Kiss remains unbeaten as Wallabies clinch series with Argentina draw
teams.body: Australia secured their first series victory on Argentinian soil despite a 28-28 draw against Los Pumas in Mendoza on Saturday. Les Kiss remains unbeaten after four Tests, though the Wallabies squandered a 14-0 lead and failed to capitalise on a two-man advantage during the final 10 minutes. A 70th-minute penalty try levelled the scores after Argentina suffered two yellow cards, but execution errors prevented a fifth straight win. Captain Harry Wilson admitted "the boys were hurting with the result" despite lifting the trophy.

teams.heading: Japan beat Canada 57-12 as Mamoru Harada scores twice in Niigata
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms ended a four-match losing streak on Saturday, overpowering Canada 57-12 at Niigata’s Denka Big Swan Stadium. Hooker Mamoru Harada crossed twice as Eddie Jones’s side ran in nine tries, including a debut score for replacement prop Takumi Inaba. Fly-half Ryunosuke Ito made his sixth consecutive start, guiding a clinical attack that established a 31-7 lead by the interval. After the clinical display, Jones turned his focus to the Pacific Nations Cup, stating: "The next game is the U.S.A., and we'll start thinking about that tomorrow."

lead.why: Japan broke a four-match losing streak with a dominant nine-try victory over Canada in Niigata, featuring a standout performance from Mamoru Harada.

teams.heading: Injured Ardie Savea exits tour following New Zealand’s 29-24 defeat in Soweto
teams.body: Captain Ardie Savea has been ruled out of Saturday's series finale in Baltimore after suffering a dislocated shoulder during the 29-24 defeat in Soweto. Savea, who scored two tries before exiting in the 30th minute, is one of nine players returning to New Zealand, with fellow injury casualties Quinn Tupaea and Luke Jacobson also departing. Coach Dave Rennie has named a 36-man squad for the American leg, insisting his side will not "use that as an excuse" despite losing their skipper.

lead.why: The loss of captain Ardie Savea to a serious shoulder injury, alongside a major squad reshuffle, is the defining story following the weekend's action.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe suffers broken jaw in Springboks' 29-24 win over New Zealand
teams.body: The Springboks secured a 2-1 series lead in Soweto on Saturday but lost Cheslin Kolbe to a broken jaw, ruling the wing out of the finale in Baltimore. Tries from Jesse Kriel and Malcolm Marx sparked a second-half comeback at FNB Stadium after the All Blacks led 17-12 following Will Jordan’s score. Rassie Erasmus apologised for his recent conduct after the five-point win, admitting his previous outburst was “not well-mannered” as he praised the tourists’ attacking threat. Damian Willemse is expected to return for the final Test.

lead.why: It combines the high-stakes match result with a major injury blow to a star player and a rare apology from the head coach.
